detail.body:
## Overview

Fixes #60030 by stabilizing standalone Triton top-p normalization when hot logits exceed the reference estimated from the first tile. Preserve the existing reference on ordinary dense rows to avoid the retained-count regression found during review.

## Claims

- Prevents overflow and the resulting keep-all mask on the sparse regression inputs.
- Preserves the current search, outlier heuristic, top-k and split paths without another vocabulary pass or host/device synchronization.
- Retains probability-space boundary-tie handling and the existing monolithic NaN fallback, and adds the reported dense input to the existing sampler suite.

## Validation

Validated against main `074c83a09` on H100 with Torch 2.13.0+cu129, Triton 3.7.1 and FlashInfer 0.6.18, reusing existing native extensions.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py
git diff --check
```

The full official sampler file passes 153 cases, with one existing ROCm-only skip. This includes the large int64 row-offset test and FlashInfer tests. All applicable project hooks pass.

The reviewer's 79 dense inputs at batch sizes 1 and 65 produce the same retained counts as main. For `(V=32768, seed=25, d=+2)`, the previous head keeps 8,505 tokens; this update and main keep 8,192, versus 8,193 in PyTorch/FP64. The new regression uses the existing comparison tolerance and fails on the previous head. Matching main is a non-regression result, not exact-CDF correctness; existing search errors remain.

Controlled real Qwen3.5-0.8B Model Runner V2 generation uses 65 simultaneous requests and actual sampler logits `(65, 248320)`. With backgrounds -200 and -100, two hot tokens and top-p 0.5, main retains the entire vocabulary and samples the two hot tokens 32/33 times. This update retains one hot token, no background, and selects it for all 65 requests. The moderate-background three-way tie control also retains one token. An additional run without the diagnostic mask observer passes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` active. These are controlled serving regressions, not language-quality evaluations.

Five alternating FP32 top-p 0.95 timing rounds give update/main latency ratios of 0.99891, 1.01009, 1.00912 and 1.01180 for `(batch, vocabulary)` shapes `(1, 32000)`, `(65, 32000)`, `(65, 151936)` and `(384, 151936)`. CUDA event/graph timing includes the same input reset in both arms, excluding allocation and compilation. The GPU was shared with training, so these are performance controls, not isolated speedup or serving-throughput claims. Both arms meet the unchanged count tolerance.

No clean full-native rebuild, triton-cpu or ROCm validation is claimed. For serving, current main's required humming-kernels 0.1.17 was provided in an isolated directory and the pinned generated FlashMLA interface was restored; existing environment packages were not modified.

## Details

The old kernel uses `avg_logit + 10 * std_logit` from the first tile as a fixed exponential reference. Later hot logits can overflow it. This update raises the reference only when a larger logit is encountered and rescales the accumulated denominator. The true maximum remains separate for the existing mask guards and probability bounds.

The earlier version always changed the reference to the true maximum. That altered dense-row rounding and exposed the existing coarse-search termination error. Keeping the sampled reference when it is sufficient avoids that added regression. Boundary duplicates are still matched in probability space, and NaN still reaches the existing invalid-pivot guard.

This does not copy #59804's gate/search rewrite or require it to land first. Its broader search corrections remain separate; this update does not claim to fix the baseline's remaining dense or split-path inaccuracies.

inline_comments.body:
Tied logits: this head keeps the whole tied group where the base and PyTorch keep the right count.

| row | this head | base | exact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 tied at 0, rest -10, p 0.3 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| 3 tied at 0, rest -20, p 0.3 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| 8190 tied at 0, one at +1e-4, p 0.5 | 8191 | 4096 | 4096 |

Deterministic, same at batch 65. In a 5,000-row fuzz with many ties, 74 rows are right on the base and wrong here, none the other way.

Possible cause: `duplicate_logit` comes from a log/exp round trip and is matched with `< 1e-9` (line 874). That fits the 8190 row (a few 1e-8 off once the reference is the max), but not the -10 rows, so I'm not sure. The split path matches in probability space instead.

inline_comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed reproductions. I reproduced both tie regressions on CUDA: the three-hot cases kept 3 instead of 1, and the large tied group kept 8191 instead of 4096. The duplicate boundary was found in probability space, but converting it back to a logit introduced enough rounding error to miss the 1e-9 equality check.

**How the rows are built**
- V/4 tokens at 1.5 + Exp(1), the rest at -Exp(1), shuffled, cast to fp32.
- p is the fp32 mass of the top V/4 tokens, then moved by `d` ulps (-4 to +4).

<details><summary>Script</summary>

```python
import sys
import numpy as np, torch

mod = "topk_topp_triton_base" if "--base" in sys.argv else "topk_topp_triton"
apply_top_k_top_p_triton = __import__(f"vllm.v1.sample.ops.{mod}", fromlist=["x"]).apply_top_k_top_p_triton

ROWS = {  # (V, seed): ulp offsets d of p from the top-V/4 mass; 79 rows that over-keep on e00cf466 and are OK on 74c5cbcd7
    (1024, 10): [1, 2],
    (1024, 13): [0],

    (1024, 26): [2],
    (1024, 30): [-2],
    (1024, 55): [0],

    (1024, 106): [1],
    (1024, 115): [0, 1],
    (1024, 149): [0],
    (1024, 171): [-2],
    (1024, 175): [1, 2, 3],
    (32768, 2): [4],
    (32768, 15): [-4],
    (32768, 17): [-1, 0],
    (32768, 18): [-3],
    (32768, 19): [-4, -3, -2, -1, 0],
    (32768, 22): [3, 4],
    (32768, 25): [1, 2],
    (32768, 29): [-1, 0, 1, 2],
    (32768, 30): [0, 1, 2],
    (32768, 32): [-3],
    (32768, 35): [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2],
    (32768, 45): [0, 1],
    (32768, 49): [0, 1],
    (32768, 50): [2, 3],
    (151936, 0): [-4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3],
    (151936, 4): [0, 1, 2, 3, 4],
    (151936, 12): [-4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2],
    (151936, 13): [-4, -3],
    (151936, 18): [-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4],
}


def quarter_row(V, seed):  # V/4 tokens at 1.5 + Exp(1), the rest at -Exp(1), shuffled
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    x = -rng.exponential(1.0, V)
    x[:V // 4] = 1.5 + rng.exponential(1.0, V // 4)
    x = rng.permutation(x).astype(np.float32)
    q = np.exp(x.astype(np.float64) - x.max()); q /= q.sum()
    return x, q


print("kernel:", mod)
for (V, seed), ds in ROWS.items():
    x, q = quarter_row(V, seed)
    cum = np.cumsum(np.sort(q)[::-1])
    p0 = np.float32(cum[V // 4 - 1])  # fp32 mass of the top V/4 tokens
    for d in ds:
        p = p0
        for _ in range(abs(d)):
            p = np.nextafter(p, np.float32(np.sign(d)))
        exact = min(int(np.searchsorted(cum, float(p)) + 1), V)
        out = apply_top_k_top_p_triton(torch.from_numpy(x[None].copy()), None, torch.tensor([float(p)]))
        kept = int(torch.isfinite(out[0]).sum())
        print(f"V={V:<6d} seed={seed:<3d} d={d:+d} p={float(p):.10f} kept={kept:<6d} exact={exact:<6d} diff={kept - exact:+d}")
```

- First block: `max_logit == -inf` forces `rescale` to 0, so `sum_exp_logits * rescale` can't turn `0 * exp(-inf - (-inf))` into NaN. Later blocks take `exp(max - new_max) <= 1`. The `logits_blk > -inf` guard in the same pass covers the all--inf-prefix case the same way.
- `max_range = 1.0 / sum_exp_logits` is exact now, since `exp(max_logit - max_logit)` is literally 1. This also removes a source of fp noise at the upper bracket edge, which my search changes on #59804 benefit from directly.
- One degenerate case to double check on purpose: all--inf row. `sum_exp_logits` stays 0, `outlier_prob` becomes exp(inf)/0, the outlier mask goes empty, and `max_range` is inf. The old code had the same shape here, so this PR doesn't regress it, but if the "clamp min to max" path above is meant to make all--inf converge to no-masking, it'd be worth one test row to pin that down.

One question on the new sparse test: your parametrization includes `(batch_size=65, background_logit=-100)`, which is exactly the corner you measured as still failing on the #59804+#60104 combination (combined mask keeps background tokens). Does this test pass on CUDA with #60104 alone? If it does, the remaining failure you saw is specific to the combination or to a different harness config, and I want to understand which before I rebase #59804 on top.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks @DimensionSTP. I tested `7e3f861c` natively on triton-cpu (x86-64, torch 2.13.0+cpu), against the base and against #59804 `0ae548aa` with this change ported on top. CPU only uses the monolithic kernel, so the CUDA split path isn't covered.

- The 12 new sparse tests pass (8 fail on the base), and the full test file passes.
- No bad rows on a sparse grid (backgrounds `finfo.min` to -30, 1 to 16 hot tokens, batch 1 to 128). The base keeps the whole row on about half.
- Same as your CUDA recheck: (65, -100) passes, and all -inf rows come back unchanged.
- One regression with tied logits, inline.

For the #59804 investigation: on CPU the combination passes all 12 cases, so the 2-hot failure looks CUDA-specific. It does fail here with 16 tokens tied at 0 on a -100 background (p = 0.5): it keeps the right 8 plus every background token. This PR alone keeps 8.

Fine with me to land this separately once the tie case is fixed or tested.
